posts.content_md: I noticed that the gelatin in the G307 formula is pre-hardened. Why is this necessary? The plates are exposed, not with a 1:1 beam ratio. So, I would think that the part of the reference beam that illuminates the plate during exposure will cause sufficient hardening between the fringes during the baking phase during development. Perhaps my question is really stupid, but I cannot figure it out.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
Wow, where are you finding all these posts Michael? LOL

Hans, if you are talking abou the 12 hour curing time, it's mostly to keep the gelatin from disolving off the glass during the sensitizing step. Remember, you can make the plain gelatin and water coating and keep for a long time before sensitizing. The key here is that after sensitizing with not only KDi but also glycerine, the dark reaction happens much faster then no glycerine at all. Not instantaneously but much faster.
